mainTopic: Whether the כתובה is from the תורה or rabbinic, and how far a husband is believed when he claims his bride was not a בתולה.
overview: The amud opens with a teaching from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. It says חכמים set the כתובה at two hundred for a בתולה and a מנה for an אלמנה, yet a husband who claims 'פתח פתוח' is believed. רבא explains that believing him does not undo the enactment, because a man does not go to the trouble of a wedding feast only to ruin it. A ברייתא then says that since the כתובה is a rabbinic enactment, it is collected only from the worst land (זיבורית), while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the כתובה is from the תורה. Another ברייתא seems to quote him saying the opposite. The גמרא answers either by switching the names, supported by his ruling about money from קפוטקיא, or by saying that only a widow's כתובה is rabbinic. Next come stories about husbands who make the claim: רב נחמן has an unmarried man flogged, and the גמרא explains how this fits with his ruling that the husband is believed. רבן גמליאל questions such a claim with a parable of a door in the dark. רבן גמליאל בר רבי washes a cloth and finds hidden blood, proving the bride was a בתולה. The amud ends as הונא מר asks רב אשי whether they should do the same, and רב אשי's answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages set up the כתובה, but the husband is believed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that חכמים fixed the כתובה at 200 for a בתולה and 100 for an אלמנה. They also believe a husband who claims he found his bride not to be a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל, who said in the name of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: The Sages set up the כתובה for Jewish women: two hundred for a בתולה and one hundred for an אלמנה. And the Sages believed the husband, so that if he says 'I found an open opening' (she was not a בתולה), he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching with two parts: חכמים set the amounts of the כתובה, and they believe the husband's claim that she was not a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Part one says the כתובה amounts come from חכמים. Part two gives the husband real power, because if he is believed, she can lose her 200. Putting these two parts side by side sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: this opens a teaching of the אמוראים
They enacted, they set up a rabbinic rule
A coin worth 100 זוז
An 'open opening': a claim that the bride was not a בתולה
Believed, trusted

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Nachman said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: that Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar:
The Sages instituted for the daughters of Israel:
phrases.notes: What they set up here is the כתובה, even though the word itself isn't said.

phrases.english: for a virgin two hundred, and for a widow one hundred.
And they believed him, that if he says
"I found an open opening", he is believed.
phrases.notes: He means he found that she was not a בתולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כתובה amounts are a rabbinic enactment (200 for a בתולה, 100 for an אלמנה), and a husband's claim of פתח פתוח is believed.

steps.title: What good is the enactment if he is believed?
steps.stepSummary: If the husband is believed so easily, the 200 can be taken away by a simple claim, so what did חכמים accomplish?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what did the Sages accomplish with their enactment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the teaching from step 1. If any husband can cancel the 200 just by saying 'פתח פתוח', the enactment seems useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the כתובה is to protect the woman. Believing the husband's word seems to hand him an easy way out. So the two halves of the teaching appear to work against each other.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is true
They accomplished, they helped
A rabbinic enactment

phrases.english: If so,
what did the Sages accomplish with their enactment?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מָה הוֹעִילוּ חֲכָמִים בְּתַקָּנָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal logic of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the husband is believed with פתח פתוח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Believing the husband would let him easily cancel the כתובה, which makes the enactment pointless.

steps.title: רבא: no one wastes his own wedding feast
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with a חזקה: a man does not go to the trouble of a wedding feast and then ruin it. So if he makes the claim, he is probably telling the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There is a חזקה (a firm assumption) that a person does not put effort into a feast and then throw it away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why believing the husband does not ruin the enactment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A groom who spent money and effort on the wedding clearly wanted this marriage. He would not lie in order to destroy it, so his claim is believed only because it is likely true. A husband who just wants to escape cannot easily use this claim, so the enactment still protects women.

keyTerms.meaning: A firm assumption about how people normally behave
Puts in effort, goes to trouble
A feast, here the wedding feast
Causes it to be lost, wastes it

steps.whatToRemember: The husband is believed with פתח פתוח because of the חזקה that a man does not waste the wedding he worked for.

phrases.english: Rava said: There is a presumption
that a person does not exert himself over a feast and then cause it to be lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: חֲזָקָה, אֵין אָדָם טוֹרֵחַ בַּסְּעוּדָה וּמַפְסִידָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Behavioral presumption (חזקה) explains why believing him does not harm the enactment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Believing the husband lets him cancel the כתובה at will.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is believed only because a man who invested in the wedding would not lie to destroy it.

steps.title: A ברייתא: collected only from the worst land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that since the כתובה is a 'קנס' of חכמים, the woman collects only from the husband's poorest land.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: Since it is a penalty of the Sages, she collects only from the poorest-quality land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about where a woman collects her כתובה from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the כתובה is rabbinic, its collection is weaker: she gets only the worst land (זיבורית). But the ברייתא calls it a 'קנס' (penalty), which seems strange, and the next step will question this.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught
Since, because
A fine or penalty
The poorest-quality land
She collects (payment)

phrases.english: It was taught: Since it is a penalty of the Sages,
she may collect only from the poorest land.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הוֹאִיל וּקְנַס חֲכָמִים הוּא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rabbinic כתובה is collected only from זיבורית.

steps.title: Why call the כתובה a penalty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'penalty' the ברייתא could mean, since a כתובה is not a punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: A penalty? What penalty is there here?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the word 'קנס' in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is a fine for wrongdoing, but a husband who marries has done nothing wrong. So the word does not fit the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: What?
A penalty (Aramaic form)

phrases.english: A penalty? What penalty?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קְנָסָא? מַאי קְנָסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The word קנס in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כתובה is not a punishment for any wrongdoing, so calling it a קנס makes no sense.

steps.title: Read it as 'enactment', not 'penalty'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא: since the כתובה is a תקנת חכמים, it is collected only from the worst land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: Since it is an enactment of the Sages, she collects only from the poorest land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing one word in the ברייתא, from 'קנס' to 'תקנה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself stays the same: she collects only from זיבורית. Only the reason is put more accurately: the כתובה is weaker because it is rabbinic, not because anyone is being punished.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the wording is being corrected
An enactment of the Sages

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְתַקָּנַת חֲכָמִים הוּא —
phrases.english: Rather, say: Since it is an enactment of the Sages,
she may collect only from the poorest land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְתַקָּנַת חֲכָמִים הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 5 by correcting the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כתובה is called a קנס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כתובה is a rabbinic תקנה, which is why it is collected only from זיבורית.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the כתובה is from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees and says the כתובה is a Torah obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A woman's כתובה is from the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a dissenting opinion: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the כתובה is from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real argument with the first opinion. If the כתובה is from the תורה, there is no reason to limit collection to the worst land.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's marriage contract payment
From the תורה, a תורה obligation

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A woman's ketubah is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dissenting opinion within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the כתובה is a תורה obligation.

steps.title: A contradiction: another ברייתא reverses רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: another ברייתא learns the כתובה from the פסוק about a מפתה, and there רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the כתובה is only rabbinic, the opposite of step 7.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבן שמעון בן גמליאל really say that? But a ברייתא teaches: 'He shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.' This fine should be like the dowry of virgins, and the dowry of virgins should be like this. From here the Sages based the idea that a woman's כתובה is from the תורה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A woman's כתובה is not from the words of the תורה, but from the words of the סופרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying the exact opposite of what he said in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second ברייתא, the חכמים learn from the פסוק that a בתולה's מוהר equals the fine of a מפתה (200), so the כתובה is from the תורה. There רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one who says it is rabbinic. The two ברייתות have flipped his position, and the גמרא must explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say? This opens a contradiction
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Dowry or bride-payment
They relied on, they based it on
Words of the Scribes, meaning rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two ברייתות. In the first, the Sages say rabbinic and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says Torah. In the second, it is the reverse.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָכִי?
phrases.english: And did Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel say this?
But isn't it taught: "He shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins":
phrases.notes: שמות 22:16, about a man who seduces a girl.

phrases.english: that this should be like the dowry of virgins,
and the dowry of virgins like this.
From here the Sages found support
for a woman's ketubah being from the Torah.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A woman's ketubah is not from the words of the Torah,
but from the words of the Scribes!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָכִי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution in step 7 with a contradicting ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view that the כתובה is from the תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying the כתובה is only rabbinic, the direct opposite.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether the כתובה is from the תורה or rabbinic affects how strongly it can be collected, such as whether it is limited to זיבורית.

steps.title: Switch the names in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction by switching which opinion belongs to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in one ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 8 with one word: switch the names in the second ברייתא. That way, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the כתובה is from the תורה in both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second ברייתא, as we have it, the חכמים say the כתובה is from the תורה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is rabbinic. If we switch the names, the חכמים hold it is rabbinic and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds it is from the תורה. That matches what he says in the first ברייתא from step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse, switch the names of who said which opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Switching the names does not change either opinion. Both views stay exactly the same. Only who said which one changes.

phrases.english: Reverse [the names].
phrases.notes: Switch the names in the second ברייתא, the one learned from the מפתה פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the attribution of opinions in one source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות have רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holding opposite views.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the second ברייתא, the names are switched, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל consistently holds that the כתובה is from the תורה.

steps.title: Why switch the second ברייתא and not the first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we chose to switch the names in the second ברייתא instead of the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you reverse the second ברייתא? Reverse the first one instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 9: the contradiction could be solved just as well by switching the names in the first ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we switched the first ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would consistently hold that the כתובה is rabbinic. So the גמרא wants a reason to prefer one switch over the other.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see, meaning: what is your reason for choosing this way?
The latter one, the second ברייתא
The former one, the first ברייתא

phrases.english: And what did you see that you reversed the latter one,
reverse the former one!
phrases.notes: The first ברייתא is the one from steps 4–7, about collecting from the poorest land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי חָזֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice made in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to switch the names in the second ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Switching either ברייתא removes the contradiction equally well, so the choice looks arbitrary.

steps.title: A משנה shows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the כתובה is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a משנה about money from קפוטקיא that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the כתובה is from the תורה, so the second ברייתא is the one to switch.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we have heard that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a woman's כתובה is from the תורה. As we learned in a משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he gives her the payment in the money of קפוטקיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its choice. Another source already shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the כתובה is from the תורה, so we switch the ברייתא that disagrees with that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a man married in קפוטקיא and later divorced in ארץ ישראל. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that he pays in the more valuable money of קפוטקיא, which treats the כתובה as a full תורה obligation. Since that matches the first ברייתא, the second ברייתא is the one we reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard him say, meaning we know his view from another source
From the תורה, a תורה-level obligation
As we learned in a משנה
The money of קפוטקיא, a place whose coins were worth more

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a standard way the גמרא decides which source to switch: keep the version that agrees with a third source.

phrases.aramaic: הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Behold, we have heard רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
who said that a woman's כתובה is from the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר —
phrases.english: As we learned: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says,
he gives her from the money of קפוטקיא.
phrases.notes: This points to a משנה later in this מסכת: a man who married in קפוטקיא pays her כתובה in that place's more valuable coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Support from a third source (a משנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The choice of which ברייתא to switch is arbitrary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה about money from קפוטקיא shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the כתובה is from the תורה, so the second ברייתא is the one to switch.

steps.title: Second answer: the ברייתא is missing words about a widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another answer: the whole second ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A virgin's כתובה is from the תורה, and only a widow's כתובה is rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say: the whole ברייתא is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and some words are missing. This is what it teaches: From here the Sages based a woman's כתובה on the תורה. A widow's כתובה is not from the תורה but from the words of the Sages, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A widow's כתובה is not from the תורה but from the words of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different way to remove the contradiction without switching any names. It says the second ברייתא is missing a line, and once we fill it in, there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the missing line is filled in, the first part of the second ברייתא talks about a virgin's כתובה, which is from the תורה. The words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל are about a widow's כתובה, which is only rabbinic. So he never says a virgin's כתובה is rabbinic, and he agrees with the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say, which introduces a second, different answer
The text is missing words
Based, found support for a law
The כתובה of a widow
From the words of the Sages, a rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. (1) Switch the names in the second ברייתא, proven by the קפוטקיא משנה. (2) The second ברייתא is missing words: a virgin's כתובה is from the תורה, and a widow's כתובה is rabbinic. Either way, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a virgin's כתובה is from the תורה.
steps.confusionAlert: In this answer, the words 'רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says' are not an argument against the Sages. They are the source for the widow rule, so the whole ברייתא follows one opinion.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא,
phrases.english: the whole [ברייתא] is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
From here the Sages based
a woman's כתובה on the Torah.
phrases.notes: In this reading, this line is about a virgin's כתובה.

phrases.english: The כתובה of a widow is not from the words of the Torah,
phrases.notes: This line and the next are words the גמרא adds because they were missing.

phrases.english: but from the words of the Sages,
as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
The כתובה of a widow is not from the words of the Torah,
but from the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate answer to the contradiction of step 8, instead of the switch in steps 9–11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words and splitting the cases (virgin versus widow)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the second ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues with the Sages and says every כתובה is rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a virgin's כתובה is from the תורה, and only a widow's כתובה is rabbinic.

steps.title: A man claims פתח פתוח before רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: a man comes before רב נחמן and claims he found an open opening, meaning his bride was not a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רב נחמן and said to him: I found an open opening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the כתובה question and begins a short story. This line sets up the man's claim, and רב נחמן responds in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim of פתח פתוח means the husband says his new wife was not a בתולה. This connects back to the teaching in step 1, where רב נחמן quoted that a husband who makes this claim is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: An open opening, a husband's claim that his bride was not a בתולה
Before him, coming to a rabbi for a ruling

phrases.english: A certain [man] who came before רב נחמן,
said to him: I found an open opening.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the כתובה is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man brings a claim of פתח פתוח to רב נחמן.

steps.title: רב נחמן orders the man to be punished
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects the man's claim and orders him flogged. If the man had never been married, how could he know what an open opening is, unless he had been with immoral women?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said about him: Flog him with palm branches. Are immoral women common around him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן does not accept the claim. Instead, he sees it as evidence against the man himself and orders him punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man had never been married before. So knowing the difference between an open and a closed opening suggests he gained that experience in a forbidden way. His own claim shows his bad behavior, so רב נחמן punishes him instead of ruling in his favor.

keyTerms.meaning: Flog him, give him lashes
Palm branches
A polite word for immoral women

steps.whatToRemember: A claim can backfire. Here, the knowledge the man needed to make his claim shows that he himself behaved badly.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: אַסְּבוּהוּ כּוּפְרֵי,
phrases.english: רב נחמן said about him: Flog him with palm branches,
are immoral women common around him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: אַסְּבוּהוּ כּוּפְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן's response to the claim in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The man's claim of פתח פתוח and his credibility
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A man who was never married should not have the experience needed to make this claim, so his claim shows that he behaved badly.

steps.title: Didn't רב נחמן say the husband is believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story from Step 14 with another ruling of רב נחמן, who said a husband claiming 'פתח פתוח' is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't רב נחמן the one who said such a husband is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. In Step 14 רב נחמן had the man flogged, but in step 1 רב נחמן himself taught that this kind of husband is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband is believed, his claim is treated as true. So why would רב נחמן punish him for making it? The two rulings of the same אמורא seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
He is believed

phrases.english: But isn't it Rav Nachman himself
who said that he is believed!
phrases.notes: He means the husband who claims he found an open opening, like the man in the story just before.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַב נַחְמָן הוּא דְּאָמַר מְהֵימַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in Step 14 using another ruling of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's order to flog the husband in Step 14
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן himself rules the husband is believed, so punishing him for the same claim seems contradictory.

steps.title: Believed, but still flogged
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: both rulings are true. The husband's claim is accepted, but he is still flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is believed, and we still flog him with palm branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction. His claim is accepted, and he also gets lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings deal with two separate things. Being believed is about his claim. The flogging is a punishment for the suspicion raised in Step 14: how does he know what an open opening is?

keyTerms.meaning: We flog / strike
Palm branches (used for the lashes)

phrases.english: He is believed,
and we flog him with palm branches.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְהֵימַן, וּמַסְּבִינַן לֵיהּ כּוּפְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15 by saying the two rulings do not cancel each other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both rulings apply together to the same person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being believed and being flogged cannot go together.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is believed about his claim and is still flogged.

steps.title: A bachelor versus a man who was married before
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי gives a different answer: the flogging is for a בחור, and being believed applies to a man who was married before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי answers: here it is a bachelor, there it is a married man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי resolves the contradiction a different way. He says the two rulings of רב נחמן are about two different kinds of husbands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who was married before could know from that marriage what a normal first time feels like, so he is believed. A בחור has no proper way to know, so his claim raises suspicion and he is flogged. Unlike Step 16, here the bachelor is not believed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Answers / resolves (a difficulty)
A young man who was never married
A man who has been married

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction in רב נחמן. Either the husband is believed and still flogged, or a בחור is flogged while a man who was married before is believed.

phrases.english: Rav Achai answers differently:
Here, it is a bachelor;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the story where the man was flogged.

phrases.english: there, it is a man who was married.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחַאי מְשַׁנֵּי: כָּאן בְּבָחוּר, כָּאן בְּנָשׂוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the קשיא of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (two different kinds of husbands)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings of רב נחמן are about the same kind of husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: Flogging is for a בחור. Being believed is for a man who was married before.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's parable of the door at night
steps.stepSummary: A man tells רבן גמליאל he found a 'פתח פתוח'. רבן גמליאל suggests the husband may have tilted his approach, and compares it to a door at night that opens only if the bar is moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man came before רבן גמליאל and said: I found an open opening. He answered: Maybe you tilted it? Here is a parable. A man walks in the dark of night. If he tilts the bar, he finds the door open. If he doesn't tilt it, he finds it locked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a similar story from earlier times. רבן גמליאל pushes back on the husband's claim with a parable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל suggests that the 'open' result may have come from how the husband approached, not from the bride's condition. Like a door in the dark that seems open only because the walker moved the bar, the husband's own action may explain what he found.

keyTerms.meaning: You tilted / turned it aside
A parable / comparison
The blackness of night
Locked

phrases.english: A certain man who came before Rabban Gamliel
said to him: I found an open opening.
He said to him: Perhaps you tilted it?
I will give you a parable:
What is this similar to?
To a man who was walking
in the blackness of night and darkness;
if he tilted it, he found it open;
phrases.notes: Picture him coming to his door in the dark and moving the bar that holds it shut.

phrases.english: if he did not tilt it, he found it locked.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about the same kind of claim as in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A claim of 'פתח פתוח' may be explained by the husband's own approach, so it does not automatically prove the bride was not a בתולה.

steps.title: Another version: he did it on purpose
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבן גמליאל suggested the husband tilted on purpose and forced the 'door and bolt', and the parable is told with 'on purpose' added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he told him: Maybe you tilted on purpose and pulled away the door and the bolt? Here is a parable. A man walks in the dark of night. If he tilts on purpose, he finds it open. If he doesn't tilt on purpose, he finds it locked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רבן גמליאל said. This time he suggests the husband did it on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the husband may simply have come in at an angle. In this version רבן גמליאל suggests the husband acted on purpose and forced his way, which is why he felt no barrier. The parable is the same, except 'on purpose' is added.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (a second version of what was said)
On purpose
Door
Bolt / bar of the door

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new story. It is the same story with רבן גמליאל, told in a second version.

phrases.english: Some say this is what he said to him:
Perhaps you tilted it on purpose,
and pulled away the door and the bolt?
I will give you a parable:
What is this similar to?
To a man who is walking
in the blackness of night and darkness;
if he tilted on purpose, he found it open;
if he did not tilt on purpose, he found it locked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, הָכִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבן גמליאל's reply in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, the 'open' result is blamed on the husband forcing his way on purpose.

steps.title: A husband and bride argue before רבן גמליאל בר רבי
steps.stepSummary: A husband tells רבן גמליאל בר רבי he found no blood, and the bride insists she was a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man came before רבן גמליאל son of רבי and said: My teacher, I was with her and found no blood. She said: My teacher, I was a בתולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a third story. The husband and the bride make opposite claims, and the next step shows how the חכם settled it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the husband's claim is about finding no blood, not about an open opening. The bride directly denies it. Whom should the judge believe? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: I had marital relations
A virgin

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי,
phrases.english: A certain man who came before Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi
said to him: My teacher,
I had relations and did not find blood.
She said to him: My teacher, I was a virgin.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about a related claim, this time about missing blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband claims no blood. The bride claims she was a בתולה.

steps.title: Washing the cloth reveals the blood
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל בר רבי has the cloth washed, finds drops of blood, and tells the husband his bride was a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Bring me that cloth. They brought it, and he soaked it in water and washed it, and found several drops of blood on it. He told the husband: Go, take possession of your acquisition.
steps.whatsHappening: The judge checks the facts himself by washing the sheet. He finds blood and rules for the bride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband said there was no blood, but the blood was there. It just could not be seen until the cloth was washed. So the husband's claim was simply wrong, and he should treat his marriage as a valid, good acquisition.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloth / sheet
He soaked it
Take possession of what you acquired (your marriage is fine)

steps.whatToRemember: A husband's claim that his bride was not a בתולה is not automatically accepted. A חכם may doubt it (רבן גמליאל's parable) or even disprove it by checking the evidence (washing the cloth).
steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows that 'I found no blood' can be a mistake, so a judge should check before a bride loses her standing as a בתולה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: הָבִיאוּ לִי אוֹתוֹ סוּדָר.
phrases.english: He said to them: Bring me that cloth.
They brought him the cloth,
and he soaked it in water and washed it,
and found on it several drops of blood.
He said to him: Go, take possession of your acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: הָבִיאוּ לִי אוֹתוֹ סוּדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument from Step 20 by checking the evidence.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The blood was there all along, so the bride was a בתולה and the husband must keep his marriage as a good acquisition.

steps.title: Should we also wash the cloth?
steps.stepSummary: הונא מר בריה דרבא from פרזקיא suggests to רב אשי that they also wash the cloth to check for hidden blood, like רבן גמליאל בר רבי did. The גמרא opens רב אשי's reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: הונא מר, son of רבא, from פרזקיא, said to רב אשי: Should we also do this? רב אשי said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: A later scholar asks whether they should copy what רבן גמליאל בר רבי did and wash the cloth to look for hidden blood. This step sets up רב אשי's answer, which comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story in the last step showed that blood can be hidden on the cloth and show up only after washing. הונא מר wants to know if this should become their regular practice too. The words 'אמר ליה' introduce רב אשי's response, so the answer itself has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: We too
Let us do so (the same thing)
From פרזקיא, the name of a place
Son of רבא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הוּנָא מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
phrases.english: Huna Mar, son of Rava, said to him
from Parzakya, to Rav Ashi:
Should we also do so?
He said to him:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הוּנָא מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מִפַּרְזִקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the washing practice from the story in step 21 should be applied in their own time.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether they too should wash the cloth to look for hidden blood of בתולים when a husband claims he found no blood.
